{{Short description|Complementary parts of argumentation}}{{More citations needed|date=June 2026}}{{DISPLAYTITLE:''Pars destruens'' and ''pars construens''}}{{Expand French |date=May 2026}}

'''''Pars destruens''''' and '''''pars construens''''' (Latin) are complementary parts of [[argumentation]]. The negative part of [[criticism|criticizing]] views is the ''pars destruens''. And the positive part of stating one's own position and [[argument]]s is the ''pars construens''.

{{DEFAULTSORT:Pars destruens pars construens}}
[[Category:Concepts in logic]]
[[Category:Philosophical logic]]
The distinction goes back to [[Francis Bacon]] and his work ''[[Novum Organum]]'' (1620). There he puts forth his inductive method that has two parts: a negative part, ''pars destruens'', that removes all prejudices and errors; and the positive part, ''pars construens'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bacone, Francesco - Enciclopedia |url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/francesco-bacone_(Dizionario-di-filosofia)/ |access-date=2026-06-21 |website=Treccani |language=it}}</ref> that is about gaining knowledge and truth.
